top_stories.title: Microsoft 365 accounts compromised at 79 organizations, no passwords needed
top_stories.summary: An attacker compromised Microsoft 365 email accounts across 79 organizations over ten weeks by replaying stolen session tokens, bypassing the need for passwords entirely. The campaign used hidden inbox rules to conceal the intrusion from victims, as documented by Huntress researchers.

top_stories.title: The 2% Problem: Three Vendors Built Agent-Identity Governance. Almost Nobody Is Using It.
top_stories.summary: SailPoint has highlighted a critical gap in enterprise AI agent deployments, noting that 79% of enterprises run AI agents in production while only 2% have deployed agent-identity governance controls. SailPoint is identified as one of three vendors that have built agent-identity governance solutions, addressing the challenge of managing non-human identities that operate autonomously without human approval steps.

top_stories.title: 1Password for Agents lets personal AI agents log in without ever seeing the password
top_stories.summary: 1Password launched "1Password for Agents," a sign-in platform enabling personal AI agents from Meta, Anthropic, OpenAI, and xAI to authenticate to services without directly accessing credentials. The product addresses non-human identity (NHI) authentication, allowing AI agents to log in securely while keeping passwords hidden from the agents themselves.

top_stories.title: Trust Is Not What It Seems — And Fraudsters Are Counting on It
top_stories.summary: The article covers how threat actors are bypassing technical security controls by using AI-assisted social engineering against help desks to obtain unauthorized access. The attack vector targets identity verification processes at help desks, directly undermining MFA resets, PAM controls, and identity verification workflows that IAM professionals are responsible for securing.

top_stories.title: AI Agents as Insider Threats: Inside Microsoft's Bet on a Unified Security Stack
top_stories.summary: Microsoft's Project Perception introduces Guardian Agents designed to monitor and contain anomalous AI agent behavior as part of a unified security stack. The initiative addresses emerging concerns around AI agents acting as insider threats, a problem directly relevant to identity governance and access control frameworks.

news.title: Forgotten AI agents may still access sensitive company data
news.summary: Arrakis Security's 2026 Autonomous Agents Threat Report found that 76% of enabled AI agents examined had not run in 60 days but still retained active credentials and connections to company systems. The analysis covered thousands of agents in customer production environments over 12 weeks, highlighting a growing access governance gap around dormant AI agent identities.

news.title: Synthetic identities leave US lenders with $2.4 billion in fraud exposure
news.summary: TransUnion's Fraud in the Age of Continuous Trust report reveals $2.4 billion in fraud exposure for US lenders from synthetic identities, with 81% of suspected digital fraud occurring during account logins and financial transactions in H1 2026. The report highlights that identity verification at onboarding is insufficient, as fraud risks persist throughout the customer relationship lifecycle.

news.title: Leaked LiteLLM Master Key Let Attackers Steal GitHub Tokens and Hijack Release Pipeline
news.summary: LiteLLM disclosed that a master key accidentally published to a public GitHub repository in late May 2026 was exploited by a threat actor to steal GitHub tokens and hijack the release pipeline. The attacker used the exposed credentials to push a malicious version of the LiteLLM Python package, representing a supply chain compromise stemming from secrets exposure.

news.title: jumpserver v4.10.20
news.summary: JumpServer released version 4.10.20 of its open-source Privileged Access Management platform. The platform provides secure access to SSH, RDP, Kubernetes, Database, and RemoteApp endpoints through a web browser for DevOps and IT teams.

news.title: Three insights you may have missed from theCUBE’s coverage of Okta’s Oktane event
news.summary: TheCUBE's coverage of Okta's Oktane event highlighted key developments in AI agent governance and identity security. The coverage focused on how enterprises need identity controls that follow AI agent actions across applications and tool calls, beyond initial authentication.

news.title: You gave your AI agent access, but who is giving it orders?
news.summary: Gen Digital has introduced an "Agent Trust Hub" designed to address security risks posed by AI agents that can be manipulated through malicious inputs to misuse their legitimate access permissions. The solution focuses on skill verification, secure connectivity, and runtime controls to govern what actions AI agents can execute within their authorized scope.

news.title: Hackers Breach Enterprise Firewalls and VPNs, Exposing Over 70,000 Credentials
news.summary: Hackers have breached enterprise firewalls and VPNs, including Fortinet FortiGate and Palo Alto Networks GlobalProtect devices, exposing over 70,000 credentials. The campaign targeted exposed network edge devices across numerous organizations worldwide, with attackers attempting further compromise of some victims.

news.title: The AI Agent Nobody Owns: Watch Expert Webinar On Your Newest Insider Threat
news.summary: A webinar addresses the security and access management risks posed by unmanaged AI agents operating within enterprise networks, specifically their ungoverned access to API keys, database credentials, and internal systems. The content focuses on the lack of identity ownership, access review, and oversight for AI agents—framing them as an emerging insider threat relevant to IAM governance practices.

news.title: Enable cross-Region fine-grained data access with AWS Lake Formation and Trusted Identity Propagation
news.summary: AWS has expanded Trusted Identity Propagation with AWS IAM Identity Center to support cross-Region functionality. The feature enables fine-grained access controls for Lake Formation-governed data across Amazon S3 and Redshift, allowing queries to execute under the actual corporate user's identity rather than a service account.

news.title: Inside the LiteLLM 1.107.0 supply chain compromise: Credential theft through Python startup hooks
news.summary: Microsoft Threat Intelligence analyzed a supply chain compromise in LiteLLM version 1.107.0 that used Python startup hooks to steal credentials. The attack involved remote code loading techniques designed to exfiltrate credentials from affected systems.

news.title: Cybersecurity Stocks Rise as Evercore Survey Flags Strengthening Demand: Okta, CrowdStrike and Palo Alto Climb 4%
news.summary: Cybersecurity stocks including Okta rose approximately 4% following an Evercore ISI quarterly survey indicating strengthening demand in the sector. The article is a financial/market report grouping Okta with CrowdStrike and Palo Alto rather than covering IAM-specific developments.

news.title: Machine speed attacks require machine speed detection and response
news.summary: Exaforce published an analysis of real-world attacks exploiting stolen credentials and MFA phishing, including cases involving stolen GitHub tokens and malicious AI installers. The report argues that the speed of modern credential-based attacks—where data exfiltration can begin within minutes—requires automated detection and containment rather than manual security team response.

news.title: eMudhra to Exit Global SSL/TLS Business After 8 Intermediate CA Keys Found Easily Guessable
news.summary: eMudhra, an Indian certificate authority, announced it will exit its global SSL/TLS certificate business after a researcher discovered that private keys for eight of its intermediate CA certificates were easily guessable and recoverable. The company's board made the decision five days after the vulnerability was reported, and eMudhra will replace affected customers' certificates with free ones from partners.

news.title: Railway Says Intruder May Have Accessed Customer Secrets, Urges Credential Rotation
news.summary: Railway, a PaaS provider, disclosed that an unauthorized third party may have accessed encrypted customer environment variables and in some cases obtained their decrypted contents. The company is urging credential rotation among affected users following the discovery of anomalous activity in its secrets storage systems.

news.title: OpenCode Flaw Lets Malicious MCP Servers Execute Code During Sign-In on Windows and WSL
news.summary: A vulnerability in the OpenCode AI coding agent allowed malicious MCP servers to execute arbitrary code during the sign-in process on Windows and WSL systems. The flaw, patched in version 1.18.33, meant injected code would run with the developer's own access privileges due to how OpenCode handles MCP server connections.

news.title: AGL hits half-million milestone with passkey adoption
news.summary: AGL has reached 500,000 passkey adoptions among its users, marking a significant milestone in its authentication modernization efforts. The company discusses its technical stack and strategic approach to implementing passkey-based authentication as part of a broader security uplift initiative.

news.title: Tech Giants Block eMudhra Certificates Tied to 8 Compromised Keys
news.summary: Major tech platforms including Google, Mozilla, and Apple have blocked certificates from Indian certificate authority eMudhra after 8 cryptographic keys were found to be compromised. The nature of the key compromise remains undetermined, prompting swift revocation action across multiple browser and platform ecosystems.

news.title: Close Identity Gaps in Software Development Before Unleashing AI
news.summary: A Dark Reading roundtable examined how AI is creating identity gaps in the software development life cycle, presenting challenges for CISOs. The discussion identified collaboration, improved identity visibility, and reduced testing costs as key strategies for addressing these security concerns.

news.title: ConnectWise Disables Cloud Backups Amid Concerns for Downstream MSPs
news.summary: ConnectWise disabled cloud backups after researchers identified attackers authenticating into Microsoft 365 tenants using ConnectWise credentials. ConnectWise has not confirmed customer impact while the incident raises concerns about credential compromise affecting downstream managed service providers.

news.title: BeyondTrust Remote Support Zero-Day Continues Trend of Exploited Edge Bugs
news.summary: BeyondTrust's Remote Support product was hit by a zero-day vulnerability, joining Ivanti, Cisco, and Palo Alto Networks in a wave of exploited edge device bugs in the same week. BeyondTrust is a PAM vendor whose Remote Support product is used by organizations to manage privileged remote access sessions.

news.title: Microsoft Patches More Than 1,400 Security Flaws
news.summary: Microsoft released a patch update addressing more than 1,400 security vulnerabilities across Windows and other software. This exceeds the previous record of approximately 1,000 fixes issued in September, which was already roughly ten times the typical monthly patch volume.

news.title: Microsoft Plugs Nearly 1,000 Security Holes
news.summary: Microsoft released a record-breaking patch batch addressing at least 974 security vulnerabilities across Windows and other software. The company attributed the increased vulnerability discovery pace to AI assistance, while security experts note organizations are struggling to prioritize and deploy the high volume of monthly fixes.
